## VaultKeeper.getActiveBackendCapabilities() method

Report the [BackendCapabilities](./vaultkeeper.backendcapabilities.md) of the active backend's configured instance — the same backend [VaultKeeper.store()](./vaultkeeper.vaultkeeper.store.md)<!-- -->, [VaultKeeper.setup()](./vaultkeeper.vaultkeeper.setup.md)<!-- -->, and [VaultKeeper.sign()](./vaultkeeper.vaultkeeper.sign.md) operate on.

**Signature:**

```typescript
getActiveBackendCapabilities(): Promise<BackendCapabilities>;
```
**Returns:**

Promise&lt;[BackendCapabilities](./vaultkeeper.backendcapabilities.md)<!-- -->&gt;

The active backend instance's capabilities.

## Exceptions

A [BackendUnavailableError](./vaultkeeper.backendunavailableerror.md) if no backend is enabled or the configured backend cannot be built.

## Remarks

Unlike the pure [VaultKeeper.activeBackendType](./vaultkeeper.vaultkeeper.activebackendtype.md) getter, this resolves (instantiates) the backend, because capabilities are a property of the configured instance, not of the type. The answer reflects configured/live state — e.g. a YubiKey slot's touch policy or 1Password's access mode — and a backend that does not implement [PresenceCapableBackend](./vaultkeeper.presencecapablebackend.md) reports the safe default (`{ presencePerUse: false }`<!-- -->) via [getBackendCapabilities()](./vaultkeeper.getbackendcapabilities.md)<!-- -->. Reading this never triggers a human-presence prompt.
